steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Oh, wow... Now that's a pretty stone.

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Ooh, it's got such a beautiful pattern, and it's really smooth. If I carve it a bit, I might be able to sell it at the market for a good price...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Say, my young friend, could you give that stone back to me?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Back to you? I found this stone in the river, what do you mean, back to you?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: It's a stone I wanted to add to my garden that took me quite a lot of effort to find. I accidentally left it here as I was returning back.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: If you give it back to me, then when my garden is restored, you can play there. How does that sound?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: No, no, no. It's yours just because you said it's yours? I saw the stone here, and I picked it up first. That means it's mine.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: *sigh* Such an unreasonable little rascal...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Alright, then how about this? I'll trade you some other treasure for that stone.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Name your price. Anything for the stone.

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Really...? Then I want a hundred, no, a thousand...?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Forget hundreds or thousands. Millions, billions, enough fame and fortune to sustain you until you're old and gray will be yours, just like that.

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Do we have a deal?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: No, no, no, the answer's still no.

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: People are always trying to take advantage. If you're okay with paying that much for this stone, it means it must be worth way more than that.

spans.text: People are always trying to take advantage. If you're okay with paying
much for this stone, it means it must be worth way more than that.

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: So I'll take real good care of it. I want to see what makes this stone so special.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: What a clever little one...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Very well, I'm in no hurry.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: When you change your mind, I'll come find you to buy that stone.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Ridiculous... Absolutely ridiculous!

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: The old man's making trouble even on his deathbed!

steps.name: Refined Woman
steps.text: Don't say that, brother. Dad's condition is getting worse by the day, and soon...

steps.name: Refined Woman
steps.text: We haven't had the time to be the most filial children. He only has the one final wish, and we should do our best to make him happy.

steps.name: Reserved Man
steps.text: Our sister's words are much kinder than yours, little brother.

steps.name: Reserved Man
steps.text: Filial piety is the greatest of virtues. You might be rich now, but do not forget your roots.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Yes, yes, yes, the two of you speak so highly of filial piety, but who was it who actually took care of him when he became ill?

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Calling in everyone because of a lost stone. If I went to Baizao to report it, the Judicial Review Office would have me locked up for obstructing official business. What am I supposed to do, huh?

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Besides... Have we ever had such a stone in our house before?

steps.name: Reserved Man
steps.text: Who knows? As the second young master of this family, surely you are the most aware of how many properties we own?

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Me? Pah! Stop trying to act all high and mighty.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: You've never come home once these past few years, then the moment Dad got ill, you came running back like a dutiful son. Who do you think you're trying to fool?

steps.name: Refined Woman
steps.text: Alright, enough arguing. If you can't help, then don't cause trouble, okay?

steps.name: Refined Woman
steps.text: That Tianshi has only just arrived. Let's wait for her to find that stone for us.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Master, this is a Tianshi from the Tianshi Bureaus, and a former deputy minister at the Judicial Review Office.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: She is here to help you find that stone. Are you willing to tell her about what happened to that treasure of yours?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: ...Hmph...

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: There's barely any devotion in those children of mine...

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Tell them that, if my stone is not found, they will not be seeing a single fen of my money.

spans.text: Tell them that, if my stone is not found, they will not be seeing a single

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Whomsoever finds that stone for me, I shall bestow upon them half my estates.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: So you are the venerable Mr. Wan.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What sort of stone is it that you lost?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: It is a stone I plucked from the river when I was young, one unique across all of Terra.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What I meant was, what sort of treasure was this stone? Was it jade, or some other precious mineral?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Neither... It was merely an ordinary stone.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Then do you know who would desire this stone?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: I do... but the one who desires it would never steal it...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Who is it? And how do you know—
Qingyan has many more questions she wishes to ask, but the old man on the bed turns his head away, unwilling to speak another word.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Where was this stone normally kept? When was the last time the residents saw it, and at what hour?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: It is normally within a small box the master had specially made, which was hidden in the deepest storeroom in the house.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: The evening before last, I was cleaning that storeroom, and everything was as it should. The next morning, I found the box smashed against the ground, and the stone inside gone...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Can I trouble you to show me where the stone was lost?

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: Come, come, please, come in! Today, I have prepared some meager wine, so as to offer you my deepest gratitude. If you are unsatisfied, please, I beg your forgiveness!

steps.name: Passionate Farmer
steps.text: Congratulations on your new home, good sir! May your fortunes and profits be grand! Here, a fowlbeast from the family coop, along with two baskets of eggs—

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: We're from the same clan and generation, cousin. We might not have been close in the past, but why be strangers now? Please, call me Brother Wan.

steps.name: Passionate Farmer
steps.text: Alright then... Brother Wan! Then take these as well. Shoes my mother worked on through the night. Please, don't mind how they look.

steps.name: Passionate Farmer
steps.text: She says she knows how much you've rushed about doing business these past few years, crossing hill and stream. The boots you buy in town might be sturdy, but they can't beat the comfort of homemade shoes.

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: Once I've settled down, I will definitely go to visit Auntie. When my home was washed away by a deluge when I was young, she trekked several hundred li to give me two sacks of millet, despite her bad back... I never forgot.

spans.text: Once I've settled down, I will definitely go to visit Auntie. When my home was washed away by a deluge when I was young, she trekked several hundred
to give me two sacks of millet, despite her bad back... I never forgot.

steps.name: Passionate Farmer
steps.text: *sigh* All you had left was a single stone. The adults thought you didn't have long to live, but nobody could've expected you were tougher than rock! You're really something, making it through all that!

steps.name: Passionate Farmer
steps.text: You made a living with your own two hands, enduring a life of hardship without complaint. You crawled your way out of the backwater, started up a business, gotten married... You've got my respect!

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: It's all just luck, really...

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: But since I was forced into such a situation, not charging headlong into the future wasn't an option. I couldn't just lay down and die, could I? I'm truly lucky to have grasped my life back. I can hardly give up now.
The youth holds his hand to his chest, his fingers clenched tight around the stone hanging at his neck.

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: Now please, sit! If we keep chatting, the braised hock will all be gone!

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: No rush, everyone, there are plenty of seats for all—Heaven above, is it really you?!

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Yes, it's me. I've come again.

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: It's been quite a while. What're you here for today? Surely not to try and buy this stone again?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: You're on the mark, I'm afraid.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Since you've already settled down, started both a family and a business... Are you willing to give me that stone now?

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: Naturally, the answer is... still no!

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: Putting aside the fact that this stone has saved my life, just wearing it to bed lets me sleep easy.

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: It's my lucky charm, so how could I give it to you? It simply will not do. Just give up already.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Very well then.

steps.name: Spirited Youth
steps.text: Huh? You're actually giving up?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: No, of course not.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I still dearly adore that stone, but I cannot seize that which another loves.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I shall wait once more, wait until you wish to put it down, at which time I shall take it away.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: This is the storeroom where valuable assets are kept?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Yes, the master kept his important account books and deeds here. Not just anyone is allowed in.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Did anyone enter on the night the stone was lost?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Unfortunately, there was a torrential downpour that night. If I remember correctly, I never saw a light turn on in this storeroom, nor did I hear any sound coming from it.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Who normally has access to this room?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: There are altogether four copies of the key to the room and the cabinets. The master's three children each have a copy, while I keep the master's copy in his stead.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: But the stone's box has its own key. The master keeps the only copy on his person at all times.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: And the box was kept on top of that standing cabinet?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: The master normally does not allow others to touch the stone. After becoming bedridden a few years ago, he has not had the time to fiddle with it either, so it has been placed somewhere out of the way.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Account books, deeds... Someone who knows what these are worth...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If a thief came in from outside, would they have sneaked over here? This residence has many more valuables that would have caught their eye.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Pardon, did you say something?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Nothing, just thinking about a case I was recently looking into, but I doubt it has any relevance to this.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Right, there's something I'd like to ask. Master Wan's three children, what sort of people are they?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: No matter what may have happened, I am merely a butler. It would be inappropriate for me to discuss the young masters' and young mistress's affairs...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Please, be at ease. I am not asking you to judge them as people, but rather simply asking what their day-to-day work is, and under what circumstances they come to visit Master Wan. That is all.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: This is for the sake of your master's final wish. You may speak freely.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: When it comes to the master's three children, if you were to only look at their achievements, they would all show great promise.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: The elder young master, oldest of them all, is a scholar. He has always boasted impressive grades, and currently holds a post at the Academy.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: The second child, the younger young master, took after his father, and has recently brought much custom to the family businesses.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: The youngest, the young mistress, is uninterested in such mundanity, dedicating herself to music. She is a musician renowned far and wide.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Based on your tone, it sounds like they have their hidden flaws?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I dare not say, I dare not... Who would care for the opinion of a lowly servant such as I?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: But... from my bystander's point of view, these three children are not particularly close to the master.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: The three of them moved out when they came of age, rarely returning even during festivities...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Does Master Wan have a bad relationship with his children?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: *sigh* Another long story, I'm afraid.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: When the master was but a shepherd boy, he had nothing. It was only after much bitter toil that he was able to start the family businesses.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: But when it came to the care of his children, he found himself willing but unable.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: It isn't hard to imagine.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Tianshi Lin, surely you do not suspect...?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I simply understand the situation a little better.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: By the way, why does your master value this stone so? Did he plan to sell it?

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: That has never been the case, as far as I know.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: That stone is the master's most precious treasure. We staff normally never have the opportunity to see it.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I once suggested taking it to the jade store to be appraised, but he scolded me with a great fury in return. I have never dared mention it again ever since.

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: I do remember one thing, though. The master once mentioned a strange individual thinking of buying the stone, one who has been thinking for several decades now.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Several decades...?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Your master mentioned finding this stone in the river several decades ago...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Does this place still exist?

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: I'll be off now, master...

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Right. Do I still owe you any wages? If so, I'll think of a way to—

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: It's all settled. The beams and pillars that survived the fire were made of top-rate cedarwood. The coffinmaker's already gathered them up. The money that's left over... I put it on the stove.

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Then... Then you can go now. And there's no need to call me 'master' anymore.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Brother Wan... You've done lots of good deeds, enough that nobody would think you any less virtuous than anyone else. How did it all go so wrong...?

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: I didn't do all that just to cultivate virtue and show off.

steps.name: Tired Farmer
steps.text: Who would've thought your good name would make you a target for vicious robbers! Damn it all, how can Heaven be so blind?! Letting such evil men go free just makes it harder for us honest folk!

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Alright, alright... That's enough of that.

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: I'm halfway to being old and gray, my family and funds scattered to the four winds. Being able to hold on to my life and... this stone... means I'm still rather lucky.
The middle-aged man holds a wooden box tight to his chest. The blood slicking his hair hides spots of gray. He is no longer young.
The 'house' he painstakingly built, brick by brick, tile by tile, all by himself for half his life, is now no more than himself and the stone.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Have I come at a bad time?

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: I'm afraid I can't offer you hospitality this time around.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Fate is a cruel, cruel mistress...

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Here for the stone again?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: At first, yes, but...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: How do you feel now? Do you believe it to be an ordinary stone?

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: I believe...

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: It's a totally ordinary stone, and I'm a totally ordinary person. A gust of wind and some drizzle is all it takes to bury us in mud.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I've met many people before, but very few of them were like you, dragging yourself out of abject poverty through sheer stubbornness and grit to achieve greatness.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Even fewer can... No, nearly nobody your age can crawl back up after losing everything in a flash.

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Are you saying I should just resign myself to fate and abandon it all? Including the stone?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: No... I simply wished to ask you one thing: Have you given up?

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Of course not!

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: I've crawled out of the gutter once, and I can do it again... I must crawl out!

spans.text: I've crawled out of the gutter once, and I can do it again... I

steps.text: The middle-aged man seems to have set his mind on something. He lifts up the box, and speaks to the kindly man solemnly.

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: You always wanted this stone, didn't you? I'll give it to you, but I'm not abandoning it. I'll come to redeem it one day.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: You mean this is to be collateral?

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: That's right. With it, I'll borrow some money from you.

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: I'll plant saplings where the trees were burnt down and lay new bricks where the walls collapsed. Right, I might be getting old, but I'm not dead yet!

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: It's just a fresh start. I've done it all once, and I can do it all again...

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: But this time, I'll do it even better!

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Hmm, I understand. But... Ah, never mind.

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Hah, don't tell me you'll only accept it if I give it to you for nothing?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I wouldn't accept it if you did.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: What I want is a totally ordinary stone. You haven't let go of your obsession with it, so this stone would be too heavy for me.
The kindly man puts down the basket on his back and sifts through it. From amongst many artifacts of porcelain and jade, he pulls out a fowlbeast crafted of pure gold.
From that golden fowlbeast, he plucks many feathers, also made of purest gold. They are heavy, and clink together with a crisp melody.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Frustrated Middle-Aged Man
steps.text: Why are you helping me?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I am accustomed to the road here. On whichever day I feel like seeing if the stone is still there or not, I need only walk two paces to come over.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: But if you were to fall into ruin and wander off with that stone, I would not know where to look for it. And that would be rather troublesome for me, don't you think?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: According to the elderly gentleman yesterday, this should be the area where he found the stone.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The river has become a graveyard... Even the trees that only sprouted after the deluge seem decades old.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: There's someone here...?

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Hey, I told you you should've come with us.

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Look at me, I became a mandarin a long time ago. It doesn't matter if it's flowers and trees or vases and pots; in Garden of Grotesqueries, when they see me, they have to bow with respect and call me—

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: Wh-What do they call you?

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: 'The Young Minister of Rains!' Heh, I told you, where it rains and where it doesn't rain in Garden of Grotesqueries is all up to me.

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: I simply need to jump in a pond and—Pow! There shall be rain!

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: Sounds really impressive.

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: What about you? What ministry are you with? What do others call you?

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: Nothi... W-Wait! They call me... 'Great Hero'!

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Great Hero? What ministry is that under? How come I've never heard of you?

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: The Great Hero is... is a big wooden box. When I'm inside it, nobody can open it!

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Th-That does sound rather impressive... But I'm a Young Minister, so why are you a 'Great' Hero? That's not right! When you come with me to the Garden of Grotesqueries, you shall be called 'Young Hero'!

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: Oh, okay...

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Look at you, did you just wake up? I'll tell you something. Once, we were both in a basket carried on someone's back. The basket's master was carrying us through the river, when you suddenly fell out of the basket—

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Tell me, what were you thinking then?

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: I... I don't really remember.

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Then do you at least remember how you 'woke up'? All of our siblings who were brought back to the Garden of Grotesqueries were awakened by the master. Who knew there'd be someone outside the Garden powerful enough to make even willful stones bow their heads!

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: What do you mean, powerful... He's just a stinky rock! And he's stupid and mean too!

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: On rainy days when you're supposed to rest, he runs out to the fields. When other workers have gone home already, he goes to the river to dig up rocks while his tummy's rumbling.

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: He said he wants to build a new house! He's got no money to get people to lay the foundations, so he's doing it himself with a shovel. He can't afford bricks, so he makes his own out of yellow clay.

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: It took him seven or eight years to build that home by himself, but he still wasn't done. As soon as it was finished, he was out the door to go do business.

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: What an idiot! Stupid rock!

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: He worked so hard on that business to get results, but once he got robbed, he had nothing left!

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: *sigh* So he did all that hard work for nothing?

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: He could have settled down and lived out the rest of his years earning an honest living. But he just wouldn't give up, and put himself through all that torture again—

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: But he's finished now that he's sick... His children are unfilial, and the family and friends who visit just want his stuff.

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: What really makes me mad is that right now, he's still blaming himself for not looking after the box! He still thinks he lost the stone!

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: It sounds like... you're a bit angry at him, but you also pity him a little? If that's the case, why did you run out here instead of staying with him?

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: Because I... I don't really know... Why does he never know when to give up?

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: I heard from some friends from outside the Garden of Grotesqueries that things like people fall into holes really easily and are unable to climb out their entire lives.

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: If that's the case, then come with me to the Garden of Grotesqueries. I'll introduce you to my brothers and sisters. They all know loads of stuff, so they can definitely help you figure things out!

steps.name: Confused Child
steps.text: Garden of Grotesqueries... What kind of place is it? Is it fun there...?

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: Of course it's fun! You definitely won't regret coming with me! I'm telling you, that place has—

steps.name: Brash Child
steps.text: This is bad, someone's here.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Wait a moment—!
Lin Qingyan reveals herself, stepping towards the big tree. The two young voices cut off abruptly.
There is nothing behind the tree, let alone a child. She looks under the bushes hidden in the tree's shadow, finding a smooth stone lying there, as quiet as a rock.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Transformed by obsession, as if become an object possessed...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What sort of obsession has ingrained itself into this stone, I wonder...

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Have you called us here because you have found the stone, Tianshi?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Not only have I found the stone, but I have also identified the robber who stole into your manse.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Please don't keep us in suspense, then. Tell us what happened, quick.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: There is no need to rush. I require a cooperative partner in deduction to explain how this stone was lost, and what connection the robber has to it.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If I may trouble you to stand here.
The man is reluctant, but ultimately acquiesces to Lin's command, standing next to the towering cabinet.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Now, use your key to open this cabinet's lock.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: What sort of trickery are you up to...?

steps.name: Reserved Man
steps.text: Cooperate with the Tianshi, brother.

steps.name: Refined Woman
steps.text: Don't dawdle. Just do as she says so we can all be at ease.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: ...Hmph.
In the end, the man continues to follow her command, taking a key from his pocket to unlock the cabinet.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: Now what?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yes, such an act would not be difficult under normal circumstances...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: But I fear it would be hard to be so nimble in working the lock if it were a dark and stormy night. A few knocks and smacks are to be expected.
Qingyan gives the cabinet a light push. A box atop it falls, smacking the man on the head before it clatters against the floor.
The box smashes open, and from it rolls a sparkling, smooth stone. She steps forward, picking it up before it rolls out of the storeroom.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: In truth, the robber was not after the stone, but rather Master Wan's legacy, locked within this cabinet.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: And in knowing where this house's true treasures were stored, they could no longer hide their avarice—

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: You... Get to the point already!

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: (Whispers) I am no mandarin of the Judicial Review Office, young master. I have no intention of getting involved in your family affairs. There is simply one thing I must remind you of.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: (Whispers) Under the Laws of Yan, the crime of theft applies equally between parents and children. Where unauthorized alteration of wills involves assets exceeding statutory thresholds, it shall constitute a felony.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: (Whispers) I ask that you act with dignity.

steps.name: Arrogant Man
steps.text: You... You...!

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Young masters... Young mistress...

steps.name: Butler
steps.text: Master Wan, he—

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Return this stone to him, posthaste.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: You and I both see true. It really is a good stone. It never abandoned you.
The old man opens and closes his lips, as if he has much he wishes to say, but ultimately, only a single sentence arises:

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: It's you.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Yes, it's me again.
That same smile hangs upon his face, the smile he wore ever since the very first time they met, when the old man was but a little boy.
The young boy plucked the stone from the river, lifting it in front of the passing stranger. As sunlight passed through it, it glowed with a wondrous luster.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: So many years... and you've visited quite a few times.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: The last time we met, you could still carry a bench to the courtyard door to enjoy a cup of tea with me.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: You've always wanted that stone. How many times have you come to ask for it, and how many times have I refused you...?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Why do you keep coming?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Because I really do adore that stone. It also happens to be just what my garden lacks.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: There was never any special reason for it. The beauty of the finest crafts of heaven and earth has never been rational.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: You are... a very strange man.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Every time I saw you off, I thought, surely he won't show up again, right?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: But you always returned, whether it took ten days, two weeks, three years, or perhaps five. I never understood how you could be so carefree every time you left empty-handed.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Every time I descend from the mountains, I gain all that I see and hear, all that I think and ponder. Even if I do not have the stone, how could you say I left empty-handed?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: All that you see and hear... So, what have you seen?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I have seen cool breezes push cirrus clouds, seen fine blossoms and young chicks, and also...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I have seen interesting men, and interesting things.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Whenever I walk home, I would think: Will he give me the stone next time?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Haha—*cough* *cough*! Keep dreaming! *cough*! You had to keep running over to my place, all because I never gave it to you.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: You call me a dreamer, but are you not the same?

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: True... We're the same.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Once I die, you won't need to keep coming over here. Pity. When my time comes, this stone will fall into your hands.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Not necessarily.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: A man's strength has its limits. Just like how I carried a basket of stones across a river back then. Despite the care I took, a stone still fell into the river, which was then found by you.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Who would have thought you would never let go of that find for the rest of your life.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Haha, ha—You knew long ago I would never let go! That's right, you knew long ago...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Yes. I knew it from the day you stood in the river.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: So... what did you hope to gain by finding me?

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Most times, I simply wished to see it. I adore it, so naturally I wanted a closer look.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: There are many stones in this land.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: But not many that are interesting. To chance upon it is destiny at work.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Thankfully... there aren't many people on this land as stubborn as you, either.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: When it comes to stubbornness, you are many li ahead of me.

spans.text: When it comes to stubbornness, you are many

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I'm afraid it's this stubbornness of yours that allows even willful stones to bow their heads.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: A man has but... a single life. From that deluge... I found my life again, thanks to the stone... and to you.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: I cannot... give up on this life of mine.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: That's right. You did it.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Despite falling into deep ravines and striking great boulders, you have never once given up.

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: I saw it all.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: This stone... I give to you. I give it to you. You...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Since you have already awakened it, allow it to choose.

steps.name: Bedridden Old Man
steps.text: Heheh... You... bothered me my entire life... for this stone... Now... I can finally be free...

steps.name: Kindly Man
steps.text: Yes. Put it down. You can put it down now.
The boy stares blankly at the stone in his palm. As sunlight passes through it, it glows with a wondrous luster. The river gently flows past, wetting his pulled-up pants.
He does not see his friends he always plays by the river with, nor does he see the man who always has a kind smile on his face.
There is no wind, no trees, no sky... He does not sense a single thing other than the river.
Time has stopped at the very moment he dredged up that stone from its waters.

steps.name: Cocky Boy
steps.text: (Melancholy smile)
The boy opens his hand, allowing the stone to fall back into the river, not thinking about whether it will sink to the river's bed, or follow its flow to the ocean deep.
He closes his eyes, and listens to the sound of the thunder, the wind, and the deluge's roar.
